name: Golden Gate Bridge
headline: length
subtitle: Suspension bridge across the Golden Gate strait, San Francisco
description: The Golden Gate Bridge is a suspension bridge carrying U.S. Route 101 and California State Route 1 across the Golden Gate strait between San Francisco and Marin County. Built under chief engineer Joseph Strauss from January 1933, it opened to vehicles on 28 May 1937 as the tallest and longest suspension bridge in the world. Its two towers stand 746 ft above the water and are 4,200 ft apart, and with its approaches the bridge runs 8,981 ft (1.7 miles) from abutment to abutment.

facts.text: Each of the two main cables is 36 3/8 in (0.92 m) thick including its outer wrapping.
The two main towers together weigh 44,000 tons (40,200,000 kg).
It held the record for the world's longest main span until the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge in New York was completed in 1964.
A movable safety net beneath the work saved 19 men during construction, but 11 workers died over the four years of building.

caveats: Britannica gives the midpoint roadway height as 256 ft (81 m) above mean high water, while the District gives a clearance of 220 ft (67 m) above mean higher high water; only the District figure is stored.
The stored weight is the 1937 as-built figure and includes the anchorages and approaches.
